name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Arbitrary Security Deposit Deduction for Normal Wear and Tear
case_dossier.summary: The landlord, Mr. Ramesh, is arbitrarily withholding Rs. 45,000 from the user's Rs. 1,00,000 security deposit for repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning after the flat was vacated in good condition following proper notice.

timeline.event: User provided proper 1-month notice to vacate the 2BHK flat.
User vacated the flat, cleared all utility bills, and handed over the keys.
Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days but failed to do so and stopped picking calls.
Landlord sent a message claiming a deduction of Rs. 45,000 for house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: WhatsApp chat acknowledging receipt of the flat in good condition
Proof of cleared electricity and water bills
evidence_needed: Copy of the signed Rent Agreement (to verify clauses regarding painting and security deposit deductions)
Written formal demand/legal notice sent to the landlord (if any)
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: The user possesses strong visual and documentary proof including move-in/out media, payment statements, and WhatsApp acknowledgments from the landlord.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You have a strong legal standing to recover your unlawfully deducted security deposit under Indian tenancy principles. Routine wear and tear like normal paint aging or cleaning is legally excluded from tenant liability, and your video and photographic evidence heavily support your claim. This is a civil dispute and a breach of contract rather than a criminal offense.

Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only required to return the property subject to reasonable wear and tear. Your comprehensive evidence, including move-in/out media and bank statements, places you in a secure position to demand your full refund.

Your immediate takeaway is to formally document your demand for the remaining security deposit using your collected proof before pursuing civil resolution.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects you from liability for changes caused by reasonable wear and tear when returning property possession.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Establishes that deposit withholding is a civil matter of contract breach, meaning criminal police complaints are not appropriate.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action (Formal Legal Notice)
action_options.details: Serve a formal written legal notice citing Section 108(B)(m) to demand the full refund of your unlawfully deducted deposit amount, attaching copies of your move-out video, WhatsApp chats, and bank statements.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Guidance
action_options.details: If the landlord fails to respond, seek free legal aid and guidance from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) via Helpline 15100. Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against a landlord.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Civil Suit Filing
action_options.details: If informal notices and DLSA guidance do not resolve the issue, file a recovery suit for the remaining security deposit before the local civil court or Small Causes Court.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can represent yourself in many lower civil forums and consumer courts without an advocate, but consulting a licensed advocate or utilizing DLSA free legal aid is recommended for drafting formal legal notices and navigating civil court procedures.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**BY SPEED POST / REGISTERED EMAIL**

**LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE**

**Date:** 08/11/2026

**To,** 
Mr. Ramesh 
[Landlord Address / Contact Details as known] 

**From,** 
[Tenant Name / Complainant] 
[Tenant Address] 
[Tenant Contact Number / Email Address] 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR UNLAWFUL WITHHOLDING AND ARBITRARY DEDUCTION OF SECURITY DEPOSIT AMOUNTING TO RS. 45,000/- IN RESPECT OF THE VACATED 2BHK FLAT.**

Sir,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, the Tenant, I do hereby serve upon you this formal Legal Demand Notice under the applicable provisions of Indian law, and submit as under:

1. That my client was a lawful tenant residing in your 2BHK flat pursuant to the terms of tenancy between you and my client. 
2. That on **1st October 2024**, my client provided proper 1-month notice to vacate the said 2BHK flat.
3. That on **31st October 2024**, my client successfully vacated the flat, cleared all utility bills (including electricity and water bills), and formally handed over the keys to you.
4. That **Early November 2024 (Within 3 days of vacation)**, you explicitly promised to refund the full security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000/- via UPI within 3 days, but failed to do so and subsequently stopped picking up phone calls from my client.
5. That **25 days post-vacation (Yesterday)**, after maintaining silence and avoiding communication for weeks, you sent a message claiming an arbitrary and unlawful deduction of Rs. 45,000/- from the total security deposit towards house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.
6. That my client is holding comprehensive evidence substantiating the good condition in which the flat was returned, including move-in photos, a move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, WhatsApp chats acknowledging receipt of the flat in good condition, and proof of cleared utility bills.

**VIOLATION OF STATUTORY PROVISIONS:**
* Your arbitrary deduction of Rs. 45,000/- for routine house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning is completely illegal, unjustified, and contrary to established legal principles governing tenancies in India.
* Under **Section 108(B)(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882**, a tenant is only required to return the property subject to reasonable wear and tear. Normal paint aging and routine cleaning constitute standard wear and tear and cannot be legally charged to a departing tenant.
* Withholding my client’s security deposit without lawful justification constitutes a civil wrong and a breach of the tenancy arrangement.

**CALL TO ACTION AND 15-DAY RECTIFICATION DEMAND:**

I, therefore, through this Notice, call upon you to remit the full unlawfully deducted amount of **Rs. 45,000/-** to my client via proper banking channels within **15 (fifteen) days** from the receipt of this Notice, failing which my client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings.

**WARNING OF FURTHER LEGAL ACTION:**

Please take notice that if you fail to comply with the demand within the stipulated 15-day period, my client reserves the right to:
1. Approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free legal aid and guidance (Helpline: 15100). *Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only and is not a forum for proceedings against a landlord.*
2. File a formal civil suit for recovery of the withheld security deposit along with applicable costs and interest before the appropriate civil court or Small Causes Court.

This Notice is issued without prejudice to my client's rights and remedies available under law.

Sincerely,

*(Signature)* 
**[Tenant Name / Complainant]** 

---

### **ANNEXURE INVENTORY (Evidence Attached):**
1. Copy of move-in photos.
2. Copy of move-out handover video.
3. Copies of all rent payment bank statements.
4. Copies of WhatsApp chats acknowledging receipt of the flat in good condition.
5. Proof of cleared electricity and water bills.

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre yaar, law and section mat batao mujhe! Yeh sab kitabein baatein hain. Video-vidio kya dikha rahe ho, flat ka halat dekha hai kya? Marble pe scratches hain, deep cleaning ka kharcha toh lagega na! Chalo theek hai, zyada mat bolo, 45,000 nahi... ek kaam karo, 25,000 kaat ke baaki le lo. Final offer hai mera, court-kachhari mat karo.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You firmly cited the relevant legal principles (Transfer of Property Act/Model Tenancy framework), distinguished wear and tear, and provided evidence (handover video and chats) with a clear deadline.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Do not accept his partial offer of settlement immediately. Reiterate that structural or cleaning costs for normal usage are the landlord's responsibility and demand the full amount.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Mr. Ramesh, normal wear and tear is legally non-deductible; please release the full Rs. 45,000 or I will escalate this to the DLSA or local authorities.
